messages:
incident-bot: [SEV2] Okta JWKS fetch errors causing intermittent token verification failures in us-east-1. Alerts from auth-proxy: 10xx errors. Paging on-call.

alice_walsh: i'm on it, looking at auth-proxy logs + jwks fetch traces. will post findings. paging bob for SRE help.

bob_nguyen: seeing repeated 502/504 from https://okta-companyname.com/.well-known/jwks.json from our edge in us-east-1. looks like intermittent 5xx, backoff kicks in and we then fail token signature verification.

alice_walsh: confirmed. token verifier logs show 'unable to fetch jwks: 502 Bad Gateway' and then downstream token checks return 401/403 for console sessions. sample logs:
```
2026-03-15T09:12:43Z auth-proxy jwks_fetch error status=502 url="https://okta-companyname.com/.well-known/jwks.json"
2026-03-15T09:12:44Z token-verify user=acct-123 error="no matching key" token_id=abc123
```

carla_pm: product - any customer impact? we have a heartbeat from metrics.

dave_support: Support reports ~1,200 failed console login attempts in last 30m from multiple customers. API calls (token introspect) mostly ok, this is concentrated on console interactive flows. Enterprise customers A and D reported issues.

frank_sre: mitigation proposal: enable local JWKS cache fallback - if remote fetch fails, use last-known JWKS for 1h and mark as degraded. Also temporarily increase jwks-fetch retry/backoff to reduce thundering.

alice_walsh: starting canary: patch auth-proxy in us-east-1 to use cached-jwks fallback for 10% of traffic. will monitor error rates and user success.

bob_nguyen: can also update routing: prefer okta endpoint via us-east-2 for jwks fetches until their us-east-1 is healthy. adding per-edge host override in our resolvers.

incident-bot: action logged: alice_walsh -> started canary jwks-cached-fallback (request id: ic-1954507890-1)

eve_success: i'm notifying affected enterprise accounts with a short note (we're prepping a status snippet). tagging customer success.

alice_walsh: canary looks good for 20 minutes, console 403s dropped ~85% for canary traffic. promoting change to 100% in us-east-1. deploying now.

bob_nguyen: also added temporary increase to jwks_cache_ttl = 3600 and set fetch_retry=2 to reduce load.

alice_walsh: after deploy at 09:42Z, overall console failures reduced to baseline. Okta still reporting intermittent 5xx on their jwks endpoint; our fallback keeps service online.

carla_pm: customer impact estimate: ~2% of overall auth traffic impacted during peak (approx 1.2k failed console logins). No data exfiltration, only availability. classification: P1->P2 downgrade. recommend postmortem.

dave_support: sending follow-up to enterprise contacts with ETA for postmortem. collecting logs and affected user list.

frank_sre: next steps: (1) keep cached-jwks fallback for 6h, (2) add circuit-breaker to prevent repeated fetches from overloading Okta endpoint, (3) add better observability: jwks fetch latency + failure rates per region.

alice_walsh: handing off to bob_nguyen for overnight watch. bob, you're on-call for the next 4h. i'll create a remediation ticket for infra to add circuit breaker and a postmortem ticket.

bob_nguyen: ack, taking over. will monitor and escalate to vendor if we see retries > 5%.

incident-bot: on-call handoff recorded: from=alice_walsh to=bob_nguyen at=1954511490

eve_success: note for comms: affected customers got workaround (temporary console retry + cleared sessions). drafting status page update now.

alice_walsh: thanks all. please add any extra notes to the incident thread. i'll open the postmortem template.

frank_sre: filing follow-up tasks: TICKET-8812 (circuit-breaker), TICKET-8813 (obs), TICKET-8814 (customer-notify)

carla_pm: tagging for PM review. want root-cause triage: okta service degradation -> jwks 5xx -> our token verifier fallback insufficient. timeline will help.

bob_nguyen: closing this thread for active mitigation; will re-open if symptoms reappear. :thumbsup:
